title.en: The Future: Continuous and Perfect (will be doing / will have done)
title.es: El futuro: continuo y perfecto (will be doing / will have done)

text.en: The future has two more forms besides the simple will. Future continuous: will be + verb-ing, an action in progress at a moment in the future: “This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Madrid.” Future perfect: will have + participle, an action finished before a point in the future: “By the time you arrive, I will have cooked dinner.” The Spanish “estaré volando” and “habré cocinado” match them closely.
text.es: El futuro tiene dos formas más además del will simple. Futuro continuo: will be + verbo-ing, una acción en marcha en un momento del futuro: «This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Madrid.» Futuro perfecto: will have + participio, una acción terminada antes de un punto del futuro: «By the time you arrive, I will have cooked dinner.» El «estaré volando» y el «habré cocinado» del español les corresponden de cerca.

rows: una acción en marcha en un momento del futuro
una acción terminada antes de un momento del futuro
una duración hasta un momento del futuro

text.en: An action in progress at a moment in the future: this time tomorrow, at nine tomorrow, next week at this time. Negative: won’t be + verb-ing.
text.es: Una acción en marcha en un momento del futuro: this time tomorrow, at nine tomorrow, next week at this time. Negación: won’t be + verbo-ing.

examples.es: This time tomorrow, I will be lying on a beach.

tr.en: This time tomorrow, I will be lying on a beach.
tr.es: Mañana a esta hora estaré tirado en una playa.

examples.es: Don't call me at eight. We will be having dinner.

tr.en: Don't call me at eight. We will be having dinner.
tr.es: No me llames a las ocho. Estaremos cenando.

text.en: A polite question about someone’s plans that does not sound like a request: “Will you be using the car tonight?” (Do you need it?)
text.es: Una pregunta cortés sobre los planes de otra persona que no suena como una petición: «Will you be using the car tonight?» (¿La vas a necesitar?)

tr.en: Will you be using the car tonight?

examples.es: What will you be doing this time next year?

tr.en: What will you be doing this time next year?
tr.es: ¿Qué estarás haciendo a esta hora el año que viene?

text.en: An action finished before a point in the future, marked by by, by the time, before. Negative: won’t have + participle.
text.es: Una acción terminada antes de un punto del futuro, con by, by the time, before. Negación: won’t have + participio.

examples.es: By the time we get there, the movie will have started.

tr.en: By the time we get there, the movie will have started.
tr.es: Para cuando lleguemos, la película ya habrá empezado.

examples.es: By Friday, we will have finished.

tr.en: By Friday, we will have finished.
tr.es: Para el viernes habremos terminado.

text.en: After by the time the future is expressed by the simple present, not will: “By the time you arrive, I will have left.”
text.es: Después de by the time el futuro se expresa con el presente simple, no con will: «By the time you arrive, I will have left.»

examples.es: By the time you arrive, I will have left.

tr.en: By the time you arrive, I will have left.
tr.es: Para cuando llegues, yo ya me habré ido.

examples.es: Will you have finished by then?

tr.en: Will you have finished by then?
tr.es: ¿Ya habrás terminado para entonces?

title.en: Future perfect continuous: will have been + verb-ing
title.es: Futuro perfecto continuo: will have been + verbo-ing

text.en: A duration lasting up to a point in the future: for + duration. It matches the Spanish “llevaré diez años trabajando”.
text.es: Una duración que llega hasta un punto del futuro: for + duración. Equivale al «llevaré diez años trabajando» del español.

examples.es: By June, I will have been working here for ten years.

tr.en: By June, I will have been working here for ten years.
tr.es: Para junio llevaré diez años trabajando aquí.

examples.es: How long will you have been studying by then?

tr.en: How long will you have been studying by then?
tr.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevarás estudiando para entonces?

text.en: After by the time, when, before there is no will: not “By the time you will arrive”, but “By the time you arrive”. Will goes only in the main clause.
text.es: Después de by the time, when, before no va will: no «By the time you will arrive», sino «By the time you arrive». Will va solo en la oración principal.

text.en: For a number or a finished result use the future perfect (simple): “By noon, she will have written three reports.” The length of the process takes the future perfect continuous: “She will have been writing all morning.”
text.es: Para un número o un resultado terminado se usa el futuro perfecto (simple): «By noon, she will have written three reports.» La duración del proceso lleva el futuro perfecto continuo: «She will have been writing all morning.»

text.en: State verbs have no continuous form here either: not “I will have been knowing”, but “I will have known her for ten years”.
text.es: Los verbos de estado tampoco tienen forma continua aquí: no «I will have been knowing», sino «I will have known her for ten years».

speak.en: The future has two more forms besides the simple «will». «Will be» plus the -ing form describes an action in progress at a moment in the future: «This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Madrid». «Will have» plus the participle describes an action finished before a point in the future: «By the time you arrive, I will have cooked dinner». After «by the time» comes the simple present, not «will». For a duration use «will have been» plus the -ing form: «By June, I will have been working here for ten years».
speak.es: El futuro tiene dos formas más además del «will» simple. «Will be» más la forma -ing describe una acción en marcha en un momento del futuro: «This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Madrid». «Will have» más el participio describe una acción terminada antes de un punto del futuro: «By the time you arrive, I will have cooked dinner». Después de «by the time» va el presente simple, no «will». Para una duración se usa «will have been» más la forma -ing: «By June, I will have been working here for ten years».

items.sentence: By the time you arrive, I ___ dinner.

why.en: “By the time” is a point in the future, and the cooking will be done by then: will have cooked.
why.es: «By the time» es un punto del futuro, y para entonces la comida ya estará hecha: will have cooked.

cooked.en: Cooked is past; “by the time you arrive” is a point in the future, so you need will have cooked.
cooked.es: Cooked es pasado; «by the time you arrive» es un punto del futuro, por eso hace falta will have cooked.

had cooked.en: Had cooked is the past perfect, an action before a point in the past; the sentence looks ahead to a point in the future.
had cooked.es: Had cooked es el pasado perfecto, una acción antes de un punto del pasado; la oración mira adelante a un punto del futuro.

examples: By the time he comes, she will have left.
By then, we will have eaten.

tr.en: By the time you arrive, I will have cooked dinner.
tr.es: Para cuando llegues, habré cocinado la cena.

items.sentence: By next June, she ___ here for ten years.

why.en: By a point in the future (next June) the ten years will be complete: will have worked.
why.es: Hasta un punto del futuro (next June) los diez años estarán completos: will have worked.

worked.en: Worked is past; next June is a point in the future, so you need will have worked.
worked.es: Worked es pasado; next June es un punto del futuro, por eso hace falta will have worked.

has worked.en: Has worked refers to the present; next June is a point in the future.
has worked.es: Has worked se refiere al presente; next June es un punto del futuro.

examples: By May, he will have lived here for a year.
By 2030, they will have been married for ten years.

tr.en: By next June, she will have worked here for ten years.
tr.es: Para el próximo junio, ella habrá trabajado aquí por diez años.

items.sentence: By the time we get there, the movie ___.

why.en: By the time we get there, the movie will already have begun: will have started.
why.es: Para cuando lleguemos, la película ya habrá empezado: will have started.

started.en: Started is past; “we get there” is a point in the future, so you need will have started.
started.es: Started es pasado; «we get there» es un punto del futuro, por eso hace falta will have started.

had started.en: Had started is the past perfect, an action before a point in the past; the sentence looks ahead to a point in the future.
had started.es: Had started es el pasado perfecto, una acción antes de un punto del pasado; la oración mira adelante a un punto del futuro.

examples: By then, the shop will have closed.
By nine, the party will have started.

tr.en: By the time we get there, the movie will have started.
tr.es: Para cuando lleguemos, la película habrá empezado.

items.sentence: By the time you ___ home, I will have left.

why.en: After by the time the simple present is used: by the time you get home.
why.es: Después de by the time se usa el presente simple: by the time you get home.

will get.en: After by the time there is no will; the will is in the main clause (will have left).
will get.es: Después de by the time no va will; el will está en la oración principal (will have left).

would get.en: Would get has a past or conditional meaning; the sentence is about the future, so you need the simple present (get).
would get.es: Would get tiene sentido de pasado o condicional; la oración trata del futuro, por eso hace falta el presente simple (get).

examples: By the time he calls, I will be asleep.
By the time we arrive, it will be dark.

tr.en: By the time you get home, I will have left.
tr.es: Para cuando llegues a casa, yo me habré ido.

why.en: A question in the future perfect: Will you have finished…?
why.es: Una pregunta en futuro perfecto: Will you have finished…?

Do.en: After Do you need the base verb (Do you finish…?); “have finished” forms the future with will.
Do.es: Después de Do hace falta el verbo base (Do you finish…?); «have finished» forma el futuro con will.

Have.en: Have you finished would be a present perfect question; “by then” gives a point in the future, so Will you have finished.
Have.es: Have you finished sería una pregunta en presente perfecto; «by then» da un punto del futuro, por eso Will you have finished.

examples: Will she have arrived by six?
Will they have left by then?

tr.en: Will you have finished by then?
tr.es: ¿Habrás terminado para entonces?

items.sentence: This time tomorrow, I ___ on a beach.

why.en: “This time tomorrow” is a moment in the future, and I will be in the middle of lying there: will be lying.
why.es: «This time tomorrow» es un momento del futuro, y entonces estaré tirado ahí: will be lying.

will have lain.en: Will have lain would mean it will already be over by then; “this time tomorrow” marks the state at that moment.
will have lain.es: Will have lain significaría que para entonces ya habrá terminado; «this time tomorrow» marca el estado en ese momento.

have been lying.en: Have been lying belongs to the present; the sentence is about a moment tomorrow.
have been lying.es: Have been lying pertenece al presente; la oración trata de un momento de mañana.

examples: This time next week, I will be working.
At nine tomorrow, she will be sleeping.

tr.en: This time tomorrow, I will be lying on a beach.
tr.es: Mañana a esta hora, estaré acostado en una playa.

items.sentence: Don't call me at eight. We ___ dinner.

why.en: At eight we will be in the middle of dinner: will be having.
why.es: A las ocho estaremos en plena cena: will be having.

will be have.en: After will be comes the -ing form (having), not the base verb.
will be have.es: Después de will be va la forma -ing (having), no el verbo base.

will have having.en: After will have comes a participle (had), not an -ing form; the continuous future needs will be having.
will have having.es: Después de will have viene un participio (had), no una forma -ing; el futuro continuo necesita will be having.

examples: Call me later. I will be working.
We will be eating at that time.

tr.en: Don't call me at eight. We will be having dinner.
tr.es: No me llames a las ocho. Estaremos cenando.

items.sentence: At six tomorrow, I will be ___ for you at the station.

why.en: After will be comes verb-ing: will be waiting.
why.es: Después de will be va verbo-ing: will be waiting.

wait.en: The base verb after will be is incorrect; you need the -ing form (waiting).
wait.es: El verbo base después de will be es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (waiting).

waited.en: “Waited” is a past form; after will be comes the -ing form (waiting).
waited.es: «Waited» es una forma de pasado; después de will be va la forma -ing (waiting).

examples: I will be waiting at six.
She will be working at nine.

tr.en: At six tomorrow, I will be waiting for you at the station.
tr.es: Mañana a las seis, te estaré esperando en la estación.

items.sentence: I ___ tomorrow. It is a holiday.

why.en: Tomorrow, in the future, I will not be working: won’t be working.
why.es: Mañana, en el futuro, no estaré trabajando: won’t be working.

haven't been working.en: Haven’t been working refers to time up to now; the sentence is about tomorrow.
haven't been working.es: Haven’t been working se refiere al tiempo hasta ahora; la oración trata de mañana.

hadn't been working.en: Hadn’t been working refers to the time before a point in the past; the sentence is about the future.
hadn't been working.es: Hadn’t been working se refiere al tiempo antes de un punto del pasado; la oración trata del futuro.

examples: She won't be working on Monday.
We won't be sleeping.

tr.en: I won't be working tomorrow. It is a holiday.
tr.es: No estaré trabajando mañana. Es día festivo.

items.sentence: What ___ you be doing this time next year?

why.en: In a question about the future, will comes first: What will you be doing…?
why.es: En una pregunta sobre el futuro, will va primero: What will you be doing…?

do.en: After do you need the base verb (What do you do…?); “be doing” forms the future with will.
do.es: Después de do hace falta el verbo base (What do you do…?); «be doing» forma el futuro con will.

did.en: Did is past; the sentence is about the future (next year).
did.es: Did es pasado; la oración trata del futuro (next year).

examples: What will she be doing at six?
Where will they be living?

tr.en: What will you be doing this time next year?
tr.es: ¿Qué estarás haciendo el próximo año a esta hora?

items.sentence: Will you ___ using the car tonight? I need it.

why.en: Will you be using…? is a polite question about the other person’s plans.
why.es: Will you be using…? es una pregunta cortés sobre los planes de la otra persona.

have.en: “Will you have using” is not correct; the continuous future needs be (will you be using).
have.es: «Will you have using» no es correcto; el futuro continuo necesita be (will you be using).

been.en: After will comes the base verb (be), not a participle (been); been goes after have.
been.es: Después de will va el verbo base (be), no un participio (been); been va después de have.

examples: Will you be going?
Will she be coming?

tr.en: Will you be using the car tonight? I need it.
tr.es: ¿Vas a usar el carro esta noche? Lo necesito.

items.sentence: By June, I ___ here for ten years.

why.en: A duration lasting up to a point in the future: will have been working.
why.es: Una duración que llega hasta un punto del futuro: will have been working.

had been working.en: Had been working marks time up to a point in the past; the sentence counts up to a point in the future (June).
had been working.es: Had been working marca el tiempo hasta un punto del pasado; la oración cuenta hasta un punto del futuro (June).

worked.en: Worked is the simple past; the sentence counts a duration up to the point in June.
worked.es: Worked es el pasado simple; la oración cuenta una duración hasta el punto de junio.

examples: By May, he will have been living here for a year.
By then, we will have been waiting for hours.

tr.en: By June, I will have been working here for ten years.
tr.es: Para junio, habré estado trabajando aquí por diez años.

items.sentence: How long ___ you have been studying by then?

why.en: A future perfect continuous question: How long will you have been studying…?
why.es: Una pregunta en futuro perfecto continuo: How long will you have been studying…?

do.en: After do you need the base verb (How long do you study…?); “have been studying” forms the future with will.
do.es: Después de do hace falta el verbo base (How long do you study…?); «have been studying» forma el futuro con will.

have.en: “Have you have been” is not a correct structure; the future needs will.
have.es: «Have you have been» no es una estructura correcta; el futuro necesita will.

examples: How long will he have been working?
How long will they have been waiting?

tr.en: How long will you have been studying by then?
tr.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo habrás estado estudiando para entonces?

items.sentence: By next Monday, she ___ three reports.

why.en: A number (three reports), a finished result by a point in the future: will have written.
why.es: Un número (tres reportes), un resultado terminado para un punto del futuro: will have written.

wrote.en: Wrote is past; next Monday is a point in the future, so you need will have written.
wrote.es: Wrote es pasado; next Monday es un punto del futuro, por eso hace falta will have written.

has written.en: Has written refers to the present; next Monday is a point in the future.
has written.es: Has written se refiere al presente; next Monday es un punto del futuro.

examples: By six, he will have read two books.
By May, they will have sold the house.

tr.en: By next Monday, she will have written three reports.
tr.es: Para el próximo lunes, ella habrá escrito tres informes.

items.sentence: I will ___ cooked dinner by six.

why.en: The future perfect is will have + participle: will have cooked.
why.es: El futuro perfecto es will have + participio: will have cooked.

be.en: Will be cooked would be a passive (it is cooked), not “I have cooked”; the finished action needs will have cooked.
be.es: Will be cooked sería una pasiva (lo cocinan), no «yo habré cocinado»; la acción terminada necesita will have cooked.

been.en: “Will been” does not exist; after will comes the base verb (have).
been.es: «Will been» no existe; después de will va el verbo base (have).

examples: I will have finished by six.
She will have left by then.

tr.en: I will have cooked dinner by six.
tr.es: Habré cocinado la cena para las seis.

items.sentence: By tonight, she ___ since six this morning.

why.en: “Since six this morning” is the start of the duration and “by tonight” the future point: will have been working.
why.es: «Since six this morning» es el inicio de la duración y «by tonight» el punto futuro: will have been working.

will be working.en: Will be working is an action at one moment; with since you need the duration up to the point.
will be working.es: Will be working es una acción en un momento; con since hace falta la duración hasta el punto.

worked.en: Worked is the simple past; by tonight is a future point and since asks for a lasting time.
worked.es: Worked es el pasado simple; by tonight es un punto futuro y since pide un tiempo que dura.

examples: By six, he will have been walking since noon.
By May, they will have been waiting since January.

tr.en: By tonight, she will have been working since six this morning.
tr.es: Para esta noche, ella habrá estado trabajando desde las seis de la mañana.

items.sentence: She ___ by the time you get home.

why.en: By the time you get home she will already have gone: will have left.
why.es: Para cuando llegues a casa, ya se habrá ido: will have left.

left.en: Left is past; “you get home” is a point in the future, so you need will have left.
left.es: Left es pasado; «you get home» es un punto del futuro, por eso hace falta will have left.

had left.en: Had left is the past perfect, an action before a point in the past; the sentence looks ahead to a point in the future.
had left.es: Had left es el pasado perfecto, una acción antes de un punto del pasado; la oración mira adelante a un punto del futuro.

examples: He will have left by then.
They will have arrived by six.

tr.en: She will have left by the time you get home.
tr.es: Ella ya se habrá ido para cuando llegues a casa.

text.es: futuro continuo: una acción en marcha en un momento del futuro

text.es: presente perfecto: un resultado reciente

text.en: future perfect continuous: a duration up to a future point
text.es: futuro perfecto continuo: una duración hasta un punto del futuro

text.en: present perfect continuous: time up to now

wrong.en: Will have been counts up to a future point (by June), not time up to now.

items.es: Will you be using the car tonight?

text.es: una pregunta cortés sobre los planes del otro: futuro continuo

text.en: passive: be + participle
text.es: pasiva: be + participio

wrong.en: “Using” is an -ing form (present participle); the passive needs a past participle; be + verb-ing is the future continuous, not the passive.

text.en: an immediate decision: simple will
text.es: una decisión inmediata: will simple

wrong.en: No decision is made here; the question asks about the other person’s plan, and will be using is more polite than will you use.
wrong.es: Aquí no se toma una decisión; la pregunta es por el plan del otro, y will be using es más cortés que will you use.

items.es: By noon, she will have written three reports.

text.es: will simple: una decisión futura

wrong.en: “By noon” shows a result finished by then, not a moment decision.
wrong.es: «By noon» muestra un resultado terminado para entonces, no una decisión del momento.
